_note: Hand-annotated mirror / reflective-surface pairs on permissively licensed Wikimedia Commons photos. Fractions of width/height. Answers follow from geometry that is certain: a wash basin projects from the wall that carries the mirror above it; a side wall running toward the camera is nearer than the back wall; a polished floor near the bottom of the photo is nearer than the far end of the hall, whatever its reflection shows.

pairs.why: Point A is on the mirror (it shows a window behind the photographer); the basin rim B sticks out from that same wall toward the camera.
The mirror is on the back wall; B is on the side wall that runs toward the camera, so it is nearer.
A is on the mirror on the back wall; the basin rim B projects from that wall toward the camera.
A is on the small wall mirror; the basin rim B projects from the wall below it toward the camera.
A is on the polished floor just in front of the camera (it reflects the far end of the hall); B is at the far end of the hall.
A is on the polished floor near the camera; B is on a person standing far down the hall.
